text:
BERT4Rec predicts selected items at their original positions using bidirectional context; shifted next-item labels would expose targets elsewhere in the input. The paper describes replacing selected positions with a reserved mask and, during inference, appending a mask and predicting from its representation. It also includes training examples with only the final item masked. [BERT4Rec paper, §3.6](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690)

The 80% mask / 10% random / 10% unchanged rule concerns corruption conditional on selecting a supervised position, not percentages of the whole sequence. Unchanged targets are intentional denoising examples; random replacements can coincidentally equal the original item. Crucial implementation distinction: the authors’ released generator supports this mixture through mask_prob=0.8, but defaults to mask_prob=1.0, replacing every selected position with a mask. Loss targets retain the original item IDs at selected positions. [Authors’ data generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py)

Implication for masking checks: track selected positions, corruption branches, and original labels explicitly. Input–target equality alone cannot establish leakage: intentional unchanged corruption, random collisions, and legitimate earlier occurrences of a repeated item can all produce equality. Actual leakage includes an uncorrupted shifted target occurrence made visible by bidirectional attention or inserting the held-out next interaction into evaluation history. Evaluation should use only permitted history plus an appended mask; with left padding, read the final mask position, never nonpadding_count−1. These checks follow from the paper’s objective and inference construction.
